page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n2 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any bundled local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the n2-standard-2 operates in the lower tiers of performance. Its stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1398.19, placing it in the bottom 25%, while its multi-core CPU score of 1837.38 falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 13.8 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 11.79 GB/sec, both in the bottom 10%. Single-threaded gzip compression is a relative bright spot, achieving an average score of 23.81 GB/sec, but other tasks like static web serving (1.95 GB/sec) and Redis SET operations (1.72 million operations per second) remain in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point to dedicated x86_64 CPU resources without the CPU credit limitations of burstable instances. However, the primary tradeoff is its low processing throughput and memory bandwidth, which limits its utility for resource-intensive applications. It is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, small-scale development environments, simple text processing, or low-throughput background tasks that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high memory or computational bandwidth.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is an entry-level general-purpose instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads, this instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data places its performance mostly in the lower percentiles, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1398.19 and a multi-core score of 1837.38. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, measuring 13.8 GB/sec for large block reads. While single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average level of 23.81 GB/sec, database operations and web serving throughput remain in the bottom 10%. This instance represents a low-cost option for dedicated CPU resources, making it suitable for lightweight workloads, basic web serving, and development environments that do not require high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-core processing.
